in_hebrew.name: סילואנוס
in_hebrew.meaning: הוא שייך ליער או יער שופע חיים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: סילואנוס הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו הוא ששייך ליער או יער שופע חיים. השם נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'סילבנוס' שפירושה יער. השם מופיע בברית החדשה ומתייחס לאדם ששמו סילבנוס, שכנראה היה נוצרי בראשית הנצרות.

in_greek.name: Σιλβανός
in_greek.meaning: Ανήκει στο δάσος ή το δάσος που ευδοκιμεί στη ζωή
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Σιλβανός είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από το ελληνικό και σημαίνει ότι ανήκει στο δάσος ή το δάσος που ευδοκιμεί στη ζωή. Το όνομα προέρχεται από τη λέξη 'Σιλβανός' που σημαίνει δάσος. Το όνομα εμφανίζεται στη Καινή Διαθήκη και αναφέρεται σε ένα πρόσωπο με το όνομα Σιλβανός, που πιθανότατα ήταν χριστιανός στις αρχές του Χριστιανισμού.

in_latin.meaning: He who belongs to the forest or forest that thrives in life

The name appears in the New Testament and refers to a person named Silvanos, who was likely a Christian in the early days of Christianity.

in_english.name: Silvanos
in_english.meaning: He who belongs to the forest or woods
in_english.long_meaning: Silvanos is a Christian name that originates from the Greek word 'silvanos', meaning 'forest' or 'woods'. The name Silvanos appears in the New Testament, specifically in the letters of Peter and Paul. It is believed to have been the name of a Christian companion of Peter and Paul. The name symbolizes a connection to nature and the spiritual significance of the forest as a place of refuge and spiritual growth. In Christian tradition, the name Silvanos is associated with qualities such as strength, resilience, and adaptability.

data.cultural_impact: The name Silvanos carries a deep cultural significance, rooted in the ancient Roman and Greek pagan beliefs. It evokes imagery of historic mythology and a connection to nature, which can be appealing to some individuals. Today, the name can represent a blend of traditional mythology and modern-day namesake.
data.spiritual_significance: In a Christian context, Silvanos' name carries a spiritual significance tied to resilience and spiritual growth, inspired by the ancient figure of Silvanus, the god of forests. The name symbolizes a deep connection to nature and the belief that even in the wild, untamed parts of the world, there is a divine presence we can trust. It may also serve as a reminder that even amidst life's complexities and uncertainties, we can find hope, peace, and guidance in the eternal and unchanging natural world.

historical_references.reference: Silvanos was a name given to certain early Christian saints, believed to have been martyred during the reign of Emperor Hadrian (117-138 AD) in Italy. The name Silvanos may have been chosen because it was similar to the name of the Roman god Silvanus, and was thus intended to confuse or distract their persecutors.
historical_references.context: Roman Empire, Italy, Christian martyrs, Roman god Silvanus

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Silvanos comes from the Acts of Silvanus, a late 4th century hagiography that recounts the life and martyrdom of a bishop named Silvanus in the region of Lycaonia in Anatolia (modern-day Turkey). The text describes Silvanus as being a Roman soldier who converted to Christianity and was subsequently martyred during the reign of Emperor Decius (249-251 AD).
historical_references.context: Anatolia, Late Roman Empire, Roman soldier, Christian martyr, Emperor Decius

It is popular in Neopagan and Nature-based spirituality circles, especially among those who follow Wicca and other earth-centered belief systems. Silvanos is frequently invoked in rituals, prayers and spells relating to the natural world, growth, and protection.
